title: [spec-gap][R-05-139] Monotonic high-water mark missing in Rust GradientTable and C routing tables (spec 11.5)
description: Spec 11.5 Monotonic Progression: Tables MUST track a high-water mark (last_now_ms) of the greatest timestamp passed to any update, prune, or lookup method; effective now_ms = max(now_ms, last_now_ms); age uses saturating subtraction. Classification: divergent (partial). Conformant: Rust NeighborTable (u64 last_seen_ms + last_now_ms + saturating, rust/lichen-node/src/routing/neighbor.rs:44,55,95-96,16-19) and Rust Router single high-water epoch (rust/lichen-node/src/routing/router.rs:182,818-834) and Python GradientTable per the spec Python note (caller-supplied nondecreasing, python/src/lichen/gradient.py:142-213). Divergent: Rust GradientTable uses u32 timestamps with NO high-water (gradient.rs:86 expires_ms u32, now_ms u32 API; only half-range wrap compensation is_expired :267-270) - a stale now_ms passed to update/lookup can make time appear to go backward. C gradient functions take u32 caller-supplied now_ms with (int32_t) half-range compares but NO high-water (lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/gradient.c:99,130,141,152). Suggested placement: add wrap-aware last_now_ms high-water to Rust GradientTable and C lichen_gradient_* entry points, or amend spec 11.5 to scope the MUST to the tables that implement it (Rust NeighborTable/Router already match the spec Rust note).
